faqs.q: What is the Closed Spelter Socket — G-417 Pattern and where is it used?
faqs.a: The Closed Spelter Socket — G-417 Pattern is a closed spelter socket to G-417 that is poured or resin-set onto the end of a wire rope to form a terminated end. It is listed in sizes 1/4″ / 6 mm to 3-3/4~4″ / 95-100 mm, each size under its own Indus part number.

faqs.q: How do I read Closed Spelter Socket — G-417 Pattern part numbers such as IH-LR-ST-CSSG417-146MM?
faqs.a: IH-LR-ST-CSSG417-146MM is the 1/4″ / 6 mm size, IH-LR-ST-CSSG417-1-5842MM the 1-5/8″ / 42 mm size and IH-LR-ST-CSSG417-3-34495-100MM the 3-3/4~4″ / 95-100 mm size. The size table lists every Indus part number with its own dimensions and rating, so quote the full part number rather than the series name.

faqs.q: Which sizes does the Closed Spelter Socket — G-417 Pattern come in?
faqs.a: Sizes on the Closed Spelter Socket — G-417 Pattern run 1/4″ / 6 mm to 3-3/4~4″ / 95-100 mm. The size table gives each one its own Indus part number and dimensions, and the [sockets & terminals shelf](/c/wire-rope-sockets-terminals) lists the neighbouring products.

faqs.q: How should I pick the size of Closed Spelter Socket — G-417 Pattern for my job?
faqs.a: Pick the Closed Spelter Socket — G-417 Pattern row whose rope size matches your rope (1/4″ / 6 mm, 5/16~3/8″ / 8~9 mm, 7/16~1/2″ / 11~12 mm and 9/16~5/8″ / 14~16 mm and others) and check the end fitting dimensions in the table. Quote the Indus part number.

faqs.q: What is the rated capacity of the Closed Spelter Socket — G-417 Pattern?
faqs.a: No load rating is published on the Closed Spelter Socket — G-417 Pattern listing, only dimensions, so we state none here. Send the load and application on the RFQ and we confirm a suitable rated option.

faqs.q: What is the Closed Spelter Socket — G-417 Pattern made from and how is it finished?
faqs.a: The Closed Spelter Socket — G-417 Pattern is made from forged steel/alloy steel and offered with these finishes: zinc plated / hot-dip galvanized. Spelter sockets are forged steel or alloy steel; the zinc or hot-dip galvanized finish protects them outdoors.

faqs.q: What standard and certificate apply to the Closed Spelter Socket — G-417 Pattern?
faqs.a: The listing names G-417 for the Closed Spelter Socket — G-417 Pattern but states no certificate. If your site needs a test certificate or third-party inspection, say so on the RFQ and we confirm what can be supplied.

faqs.q: What do I use with the Closed Spelter Socket — G-417 Pattern?
faqs.a: The Closed Spelter Socket — G-417 Pattern goes on the end of [steel wire rope](/c/steel-wire-rope). The alternative terminations are an eye closed with [wire rope clips](/c/wire-rope-clips) or [ferrules and sleeves](/c/wire-rope-ferrules-sleeves), and thimbles for those eyes are on the [wire rope thimbles](/c/wire-rope-thimbles). [Our guide to open and closed spelter sockets](/blog/spelter-sockets-open-vs-closed) sets the two socket types side by side.

faqs.q: How do I install and check the Closed Spelter Socket — G-417 Pattern?
faqs.a: The Closed Spelter Socket — G-417 Pattern is set onto the rope by the maker's procedure for the rope size, and a finished termination should be checked by a competent person before use. [Our guide to open and closed spelter sockets](/blog/spelter-sockets-open-vs-closed) covers the choice.
